title: Lesson 5: Pleasant, Painful, and Neutral Feelings — The Worldling's Second Arrow

suttaRef.title: The Arrow (SN 36.6 - Saṃyutta Nikāya)
suttaRef.excerptPali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, purisaṃ sallena vijjheyya. Tamenaṃ dutiyena sallena anuvedhaṃ vijjheyya. Evañhi so, bhikkhave, puriso dvisallena vedanaṃ vediyetha... Assutavā puthujjano dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno socati rodati paridevati... So dvemā vedanā vedayati — kāyikañca, cetasikañca.
suttaRef.excerptTranslation: Suppose, monks, a person were pierced by a dart. And right after that, pierced by a second dart. That person would experience the pain of two darts... When an uninstructed worldling is touched by painful feeling, he weeps and grieves... He experiences two kinds of feelings: a bodily one and a mental one.

pariyatti.shortSummary: Feeling is the vital link in Dependent Origination: Contact conditions Feeling, Feeling conditions Craving. The uninstructed worldling responds to physical pain with emotional despair, shooting a second arrow into consciousness. The noble disciple bears the first arrow without firing the second.

coreConcepts.definition: Pleasant feeling (*Sukha*), painful feeling (*Dukkha*), and neutral feeling (*Adukkhamasukha*).
Inherent physical sensation registered through sensory nerves without emotional overlay.
Self-inflicted emotional torment: rage, victimhood, self-pity, and anxious resistance.

pariyatti.expositionMarkdown:
### 1. The Critical Pivot in Dependent Origination
We cannot close eyes and ears permanently. Senses will inevitably meet stimuli, generating feeling. **The exact pivot where liberation occurs is between Feeling and Craving.**

### 2. Disarming the Second Arrow
Pain in the knee during sitting is mere sensation. Suffering only ignites when the mind screams: 'Why is this happening to ME?'. Observing sensation objectively breaks emotional agony instantly.

commonMisconceptions.mistake: Vipassanā aims to turn you into an insensitive stone block devoid of sensation.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Awakened beings feel bodily pain keenly; their minds simply harbor zero aversion or anxiety.

commonMisconceptions.mistake: Gritting teeth and fighting pain with aggressive willpower.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Aggressive endurance is subtle aversion. Vipassanā softly observes sensations arising and decaying.

patipatti.practiceGuide:
1. When leg aches in meditation: Pause before shifting. For 3 minutes inspect the focal center: heat, throbbing, vibration. Notice its fluid constant flux.
2. Upon annoying messages: Stop, note 'painful mental feeling present', breathe 3 times, refuse to reply while arrow is lodged in heart.
patipatti.suggestedVirtue: Serene acceptance of unpleasant sensation without blame or complaint.

pativedha.reflectionPrompt: Was there a moment today where you caught and intercepted the second arrow before it mutated into outright rage?
selfAuditChecklist: I registered bodily discomfort without snapping or irritable reactivity.
I refrained from binge-eating or digital escapism just to evade loneliness.
I witnessed the moment-to-moment flux of an itch or ache on my body.
